version.changelog:
- Initial release of the email skill for sending and receiving emails via HTTP API.
- Supports signing up for services, entering verification codes, sending notifications or reports, searching emails, downloading attachments, and general inbox management.
- Requires environment variables: MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, and MAILS_MAILBOX.
- Includes API endpoints for inbox listing, reading and deleting emails, waiting for verification codes, sending emails (with attachments), and checking health/status.
- Enforces that outgoing emails must use the configured MAILS_MAILBOX as the sender.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mails-for-agent
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides a standard interface for an AI agent to interact with an email service via an HTTP API using curl. The functionality described in SKILL.md, including inbox management, sending emails, and retrieving verification codes, is consistent with the stated purpose of enabling email-based workflows. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution was found.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions are consistent with an email API client: it only asks for an API URL, an auth token, a mailbox identifier, and curl, which match its stated purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name/description describe an HTTP-based email interface and the declared requirements (MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, MAILS_MAILBOX, curl) are exactly what an email-API integration needs. There are no unrelated binaries or credentials requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains concrete curl commands that only reference the declared env vars and the provided API endpoints (inbox, email, send, attachment, code). The instructions do write downloads to disk (download attachment -o filename.pdf) and instruct deleting emails, which is expected for mailbox management. There are no steps that read unrelated files or other environment variables.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or code is included (instruction-only skill). That minimizes disk-write/execution risk; the skill relies on curl being available as declared.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The three required env vars are proportionate and relevant: an API URL, an auth token (primaryEnv), and the mailbox address. No unrelated secrets or system config paths are requested. As with any token, scope should be minimized by the service owner.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false (good). The skill is user-invocable and allows normal model invocation (default), so an agent could autonomously call the email API when permitted — this is expected for an agent-facing skill but increases sensitivity because it grants the agent live access to send/receive email for the configured mailbox.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it gives an agent programmatic read/write access to the mailbox identified by MAILS_MAILBOX using MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN and MAILS_API_URL. Before installing: 1) Only provide a token with minimal scope for this mailbox (do not reuse a general-purpose token). 2) Prefer using a disposable or dedicated mailbox to avoid exposing your primary email. 3) Verify MAILS_API_URL is a trusted service endpoint (an untrusted URL could collect all messages). 4) Be aware the agent can download attachments and delete messages — monitor activity and logs and be ready to revoke the token if you see abuse. 5) Test with a throwaway account first. If you need the agent to only read but not send or delete, see if the service can issue a read-only token and use that instead.
